questions.question: What is the purpose of configuring threshold monitoring in Event Management?

options.text: To limit the number of alerts generated per day
To generate alerts when metrics exceed defined bounds
To control MID Server memory usage

explanation.correct: Threshold monitoring allows you to define bounds for metrics. When metrics exceed these thresholds, events are generated that can be converted to alerts for remediation. This enables proactive monitoring based on metric values. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/configure-threshold-monitoring.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Thresholds control alert generation based on metric values, not daily limits
MID Server memory is managed separately
Job scheduling is separate from threshold monitoring

source.excerpt: Configure threshold monitoring to generate events when metric values exceed defined bounds.

questions.question: Which plugin must be activated for Azure Metrics and AWS CloudWatch Metrics connectors to display in Event Management?

explanation.correct: The Azure Metrics and AWS CloudWatch Metrics connectors display in the base system only when the Operational Intelligence plugin (com.snc.sa.metric) is activated. This plugin provides metric intelligence capabilities. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Event Management Core is the base, not specifically for metric connectors
Cloud Management is a different plugin
ITOM Visibility is not the required plugin for these connectors

source.excerpt: The Azure Metrics and AWS CloudWatch Metrics connectors display in the base system only when the Operational Intelligence plugin (com.snc.sa.metric) is activated.

questions.question: What authentication method can be configured for the MID Web Server extension when receiving metric data?

explanation.correct: The MID Web Server extension supports key-based authentication. You generate an authentication token using HMAC (Hash Message Authentication Code) which is sent in the Authorization header of incoming requests. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/configure-mid-web-server-extension-metric-data.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Key-based auth uses HMAC tokens, not username/password
OAuth 2.0 is one option but key-based is specifically documented
SAML is not the primary method for MID Web Server metric data

source.excerpt: Provide added security to your MID Web Server extension by using key-based authentication. Generate an authentication token to be sent in the Authorization header of incoming client requests.

questions.question: When configuring key-based MID Web Server authentication for metrics, what is the maximum time difference allowed between the timestamp in the request and the MID Server time?

explanation.correct: For the timestamp requirement in key-based authentication, a valid timestamp is required for authenticating the request. Ensure that the timestamp is within 15 minutes of the MID Server. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/configure-mid-web-server-extension-metric-data.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: 5 minutes is too restrictive; the limit is 15 minutes
10 minutes is below the actual 15-minute limit

source.excerpt: For the timestamp requirement, a valid timestamp that uses HTTP date header is required for authenticating the request. Ensure that the timestamp is within 15 minutes of the MID Server.

questions.question: What is the API endpoint path for sending raw metric data to the MID Web Server?

explanation.correct: The path to the web service API for sending raw metric data is /api/mid/sa/metrics. The full URL format is https://<MID Server IP address>:<port number>/api/mid/sa/metrics. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/configure-mid-web-server-extension-metric-data.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is not the correct API path
This is not the correct API path
This is not the correct API path

source.excerpt: Path to a web service API for sending raw data: URL format: https://<MID Server IP address>:<port number>/api/mid/sa/metrics

questions.question: Which two elements are used when constructing the HMAC signature string for MID Web Server authentication? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: The HMAC signature string is constructed using: HTTP-Verb, Content-Type, Date, and Request-Path. These elements are concatenated with newline characters. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/task/configure-mid-web-server-extension-metric-data.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Instance URL is not part of the signature string; Request-Path is used
User Agent is not included in the HMAC signature

source.excerpt: Use the following request elements to generate the required string: HTTP-Verb, Content-Type, Date, and Request-Path.
